proposed_from.topic: All-tests nuisance-limited spectral detection frontier for conditional distributional treatment effects. In the iid binary-treatment unconfounded model with fixed overlap, bounded characteristic kernels, uniform continuous covariates, and explicit Holder classes for the propensity and conditional outcome laws, define the SCoDiTE RKHS norm separation problem and its answer-open minimax boundary over covariance eigen-decay and source classes. Derive the regime-wise equality or strict gap from the known-propensity experiment using paired fuzzy likelihood mixtures and procedures that include higher-order correction; characterize by an iff spectral criterion when the named SKCD-MMD or regularized SKCD-Wald test is optimal; and construct a jointly calibrated adaptive regularization-grid test. Consumer: the 401(k) conditional wealth-distribution analysis, where the theorem replaces heuristic whitening with a size-valid choice and identifies regimes in which whitening loses to MMD. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A bounded unbiased Hilbert-feature oracle test and matching root-n lower bound were derived. For source exponent at most one-half and total nuisance smoothness below half the dimension, legal continuous-covariate Bernoulli fuzzy mixtures satisfy the exact null, have identical one-record mixtures, and yield a slower all-tests separation lower bound; finite enumeration checked positivity, normalization, and cancellation. Checks also exposed that centered characteristic kernels may not make the RKHS null identical to conditional homogeneity, so the target interpretation must remain kernel-specific. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Match the SCoDiTE boundary under arbitrary bounded covariate density, determining whether the known-design low-smoothness radius is attainable or a larger occupancy obstruction governs the exact null. EARLY KILL TEST: In one dimension with a polynomial Fourier kernel and rough nuisance smoothness 0.2 per nuisance, audit an upper procedure at the predicted resolution and verify that rough-density null mixtures remain inside the exact SCoDiTE null; failure must pivot the design regime. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest causal result is Jain and Luedtke's first-order SCoDiTE theory; the closest smooth causal frontier is Kennedy et al.'s scalar CATE theorem; and the closest arbitrary-density higher-order method is Liu et al.'s arXiv:1705.07577v5 empirical-HOIF construction for scalar missing-at-random and doubly robust functionals with \(k=o(n)\). The flagship object is the arbitrary-design all-tests radius for the kernel-specific SCoDiTE norm. It tests the explicit candidate \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{occ}}\), in which \(\chi_{n,h,j}\) measures primitive pair occupancy and \(\Gamma_n(h;P_X)\) measures the resulting block-Gram inflation. The converse uses fully displayed conditional masses: \(p_\omega=(1+r_Au_\omega)(1+s_Yv_\omega)/4\) has \(U=0\), whereas \(q_\omega=(1+r_Au_\omega-s_Yv_\omega+r_As_Yu_\omega v_\omega)/4\) is nonfactorizing and yields \(U_\omega=2u_\omega v_\omega b_Y/(1-u_\omega^2)\neq0\). Disjoint supports and shared signs give exact equality of the uniform one-record mixtures. Separate quantitative bounds derive positivity, overlap, propensity and arm-embedding Hölder membership, nonzero \(\Psi\), a covariance-operator sandwich and polynomial eigen-profile, the \(0<s\le1/2\) source norm, and bounded \(n\)-record affinity at \(h\asymp n^{-2/(2t+d)}\); none of these memberships is assumed. The fact that the rough optimizer can have \(K_h>n\) only shows that Liu et al. do not subsume the question; it is not evidence that the candidate penalty is correct. The high-smoothness upper theorem is stated over the declared model without an implicit submodel assumption, and its matching parametric lower bound is separated behind an explicit regular constant-contrast richness premise. The Fourier quotient-null theorem prevents characteristicness from being invoked after covariate smoothing without full covariate spectral support.

seed_details.title: Arbitrary-design SCoDiTE minimax frontier and the high-rank occupancy obstruction
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; Theorems 1 and 2; Section 4.2; Remark 11; Appendix B.8; Discussion
seed_details.anchor_read: The localized fuzzy-hypothesis lower bound and the local higher-order correction were read together. The proof's first density-sensitive step is inversion of the local population Gram matrix; the paper states that its rate is attained only when the design density is known or estimated accurately enough.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace the known-density projection inverse by an empirical, block-local higher-order construction at a target rank that may exceed the sample size, or prove that this rank barrier changes the radius.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for arbitrary bounded design density, higher-order causal testing, SCoDiTE minimax testing, and random-design quadratic functionals found empirical higher-order influence functions and random-design variance estimation, but no SCoDiTE separation theorem in the rough regime.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The kernel is not a default matched-converse exercise: the M7 component asks whether a rate proved under uniform design is uniform over the full positive density band, with an occupancy obstruction as the alternative answer.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from empirical higher-order influence functions because a sample Gram matrix removes density estimation. Rebuttal: the published empirical construction requires projection dimension \(M\lesssim n/\log^3 n\), whereas the rough-regime balance here requires \(M\asymp n^{2d/(2t+d)}>n\) when \(t<d/2\).

seed_details.title: Strict known-propensity versus unknown-propensity SCoDiTE detection gap
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; Proposition 1; Lemma 1; Theorems 1 and 2; Discussion
seed_details.anchor_read: The SCoDiTE moment, its Hilbert efficient influence function, the product-rate weak-convergence theorem, and the fixed-alternative test were read. The first changed step is to replace pointwise asymptotic linearity by uniform testing risk and to compare two experiments differing only by disclosure of the propensity.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Build paired fuzzy likelihood mixtures whose individual null laws satisfy the exact SCoDiTE null and whose one-record mixtures agree, then transfer source membership through a covariance sandwich.
seed_details.destination_search: The exact target--method search returned the Jain--Luedtke paper and conditional-distribution estimators, but no all-tests causal RKHS separation radius.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is a genuine experiment-comparison frontier with an all-tests lower bound, not an estimator-specific product-remainder calculation.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the CATE fuzzy construction because a Hilbert feature is only a vector-valued outcome. Rebuttal: exact membership of every null mixture component, covariance-dependent source membership, and a nonzero embedded signal are additional constraints absent from the scalar construction.

seed_details.title: Necessary-and-sufficient spectral optimality criterion for SKCD--MMD and SKCD--Wald
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; Theorems 3.1 and 3.2; Corollaries 3.3 and 3.4; Section 4; adaptive-test theorems; conclusion
seed_details.anchor_read: The direct two-sample source-class lower bound, the regularized statistic, effective-dimension power calculation, and adaptive aggregation were read. Its loss is triangular-discrimination separation, not the RKHS norm used by SCoDiTE.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Insert eigenwise higher-order nuisance remainder and empirical covariance perturbation into the sequence reduction before optimizing the filter.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for causal spectral regularization with fitted nuisances returned fixed-regularization SKCD and direct two-sample spectral tests, but no causal iff criterion.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The proposal does not import the direct two-sample exponent; it first derives the causal all-tests modulus and then asks for an iff method-optimality criterion.
seed_details.red_team: Hagrass, Sriperumbudur, and Li already prove that whitening is minimax. Rebuttal: their separation metric and direct experiment differ; under RKHS-norm separation the oracle boundary is root-\(n\), so the unresolved comparison is nuisance amplification and local power, not their published exponent ordering.

seed_details.anchor_read: The finite-sample Monte Carlo calibration, dependent-test aggregation, Sobolev oracle rate, and conclusion were read. Exchangeability of directly observed samples drives its calibration.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace permutation exchangeability by a uniform coupling of cross-fitted Hilbert influence features and estimated covariance operators over the entire grid.
seed_details.destination_search: No jointly calibrated causal SCoDiTE grid over both higher-order rank and covariance regularization was located.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The grid is not a bare tuning heuristic: the required claim includes simultaneous size, an oracle inequality, and an adaptation converse.
seed_details.red_team: Bonferroni aggregation makes this routine. Rebuttal: pointwise validity of fitted-nuisance statistics does not provide uniform validity when small regularizers amplify shared nuisance and eigenvector errors, and the sharp adaptation penalty remains unknown.

seed_details.title: Non-Gaussian limit law for a high-rank higher-order SCoDiTE statistic
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; efficient influence-function lemma; Theorems 1 and 2; Discussion
seed_details.anchor_read: The Hilbert influence expansion and fixed-operator weak limit were read. Liu et al. were then opened as the method exemplar: their sample-Gram recursion and Hoeffding analysis require \(M\lesssim n/\log^3 n\), leaving the rank-larger-than-sample regime uncovered.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Derive the joint degenerate \(U\)-statistic limit when the approximation rank crosses \(n\), using local collisions rather than an invertible global Gram matrix.
seed_details.destination_search: The nearest limit results concern scalar higher-order functionals or first-order Hilbert estimators; no high-rank Hilbert quadratic limit for SCoDiTE was found.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This deliberately occupies the limit-law lane; it is not relabeled rate theory, although the candidate is dropped because high-rank empirical projection is presently too fragile.
seed_details.red_team: This is merely a vector-valued version of a standard degenerate \(U\)-statistic limit. Rebuttal: the diverging effective rank, empirical projection, and covariance filter interact, so neither a fixed-kernel chaos limit nor the published scalar variance bound applies.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; local asymptotic minimax theorem; SKCD test construction; Discussion
seed_details.anchor_read: The SCoDiTE local asymptotic minimax theorem and fixed-operator test were read. Luedtke and Chung were then opened as the method exemplar; their Hilbert efficiency result concerns estimation loss, not a composite shrinking-null power envelope.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Pass from Hilbert estimation convolution to a Gaussian-shift testing experiment with source-constrained directions and a shrinking covariance filter.
seed_details.destination_search: No published local maximin envelope for conditional distributional causal effects with a shrinking inverse-covariance operator was found.
